stories.title: Europe will take part in US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, French FM says
stories.description: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, adding that Europeans will be represented at the summit. The talks will take place under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday.
stories.excerpt: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, adding that Europeans will be represented at the summit. The talks will take place under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday. Europe will be represented at upcoming US-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said Sunday. "The Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot told RTL radio. His comment came after President Donald Trump stoked fears of a US pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe". Up to now, the talks scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday had been framed as a trilateral format at the level of officials, not leaders, from Ukraine, Russia and the United States. The identities of who would take part have not been made public.

stories.title: Akdagmadeni wakes up to white blanket as snow reaches Yozgat
stories.description: Snow blanketed the higher elevations and forested areas of district, and drone footage shows the white landscape from above
stories.excerpt: Snowfall hit Akdagmadeni, a district of Yozgat in central Türkiye, giving the area a wintry look and prompting a series of photographs and drone images of the changing scenery. The snow began falling in the district early this morning and gradually changed the appearance of the surrounding landscape. The higher elevations around Akdagmadeni were blanketed in white, with snow covering the hillsides and ridges that overlook the district. Forested areas in the district also turned white as snow settled on the trees and the ground beneath them. Drone cameras captured the snow-covered areas, offering wide aerial views that are difficult to see from ground level. From above, the contrast between the white ground and the darker tree lines is clearly visible across the forested slopes. The images show how the snowfall has changed the look of the district’s natural surroundings in a matter of hours. Akdagmadeni lies in Yozgat, an inland province where snowfall is common during the colder months

stories.title: Erzurum hosts 10th off-road festival with nearly 50 vehicles
stories.description: Nearly 60 clubs took part, and a women’s class, held for the third time in Türkiye, saw seven women's races on a muddy 2,000-meter track in the cold
stories.excerpt: Erzurum, a city in eastern Türkiye, hosted the 10th Erzurum Culture and Tourism Off-Road Festival, with nearly 60 clubs and nearly 50 vehicles taking part. The races, organized by the Dadas Off-Road Sports Club with the support of the Governorship, the Metropolitan Municipality and the Provincial Directorate of Culture and Tourism, were held on a challenging, rugged 2,000-meter track in the Yakutiye district. Pilots trying to get past obstacles in their 4x4 vehicles on the muddy, highly difficult terrain completed the race in two laps. Ignoring the cold weather and occasional snowfall, the pilots battled to reach the finish line in the shortest time possible. Residents who came to the event area watched the races, which featured entertaining moments, with interest. Provincial Director of Culture and Tourism Ahmet Yer told reporters that they held the 10th edition of the festival in Erzurum this year. Speaking about the festival’s contributions, Yer said more than 100 athletes took part

stories.excerpt: As the SPLM conducts its primaries ahead of the December 2026 General Elections, I believe we need to have an honest conversation about leadership and what we expect from those seeking public office. Across South Sudan’s ten states and three administrative areas, many people are looking for leaders who can make a difference in their daily lives. They want roads that connect communities, hospitals that provide care, schools where children can learn and clean water for their families. They also want leaders who listen when they raise concerns and take responsibility when things go wrong. This is not too much to ask. It is what leadership should be about. Those seeking to become governors or chief administrators must understand that public office is not a reward or a personal achievement. It comes with the responsibility to serve the people. stories.title: 'That's Reece' - World Cup semi-final brings out best and worst of Walsh
stories.description: On a fractious night in Sydney that ended with Australia reaching yet another Men's Rugby League World Cup final, it was no surprise to see Reece Walsh centre stage – for better or worse.
stories.excerpt: On a fractious night in Sydney, it was no surprise to see Reece Walsh at the centre of the action – for better or worse. The full-back scored three of Australia's eight tries as they beat Samoa 44-12 to reach a 16th successive men's Rugby League World Cup final. His two second-half tries helped keep a burgeoning Samoa comeback at bay, while his first-half effort demonstrated his skill and showmanship. On 32 minutes, Walsh administered the harshest of punishments on Samoa for the smallest amount of defensive laxity, racing through the tiniest gap on the left to score. In front of approximately 40,000 spectators, the Kangaroos' number one celebrated with a backflip. It was the kind of celebration you expect from a man once christened by Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys as "the Justin Bieber of rugby league" and "charisma on steroids". stories.title: OPINION: How opposition divisions could hand Ruto an overwhelming 2027 victory
stories.description: Kenya’s presidential election is effectively a winner-takes-all contest, provided the winning candidate secures more than 50 per cent of valid votes cast and meets the constitutional geographical distribution threshold. A candidate does not need 80 per cent of Kenyans to support him. He needs his opponents to divide their support.
stories.excerpt: The past few weeks have seen four political parties file notices with the Registrar of Political Parties seeking to change their names, symbols and colours. On Friday afternoon, Edwin Sifuna unveiled the newly rebranded Linda Mwananchi Party’s “dream team”, naming Godfrey Osotsi as chairperson, with Kawira Mwangaza and Faith Odhiambo as deputies. He promised a party with a presence in all 47 counties by November 30. At almost the same hour, Kalonzo Musyoka was being heckled in Lavington, with some of his Ukambani allies accused of opening the door for President William Ruto. These events capture the contradiction within Kenya’s opposition. While leaders talk about removing Ruto from power, their political activities increasingly appear designed to undermine one another. rejected.description: With 99 percent of votes counted, President Cyril Ramaphosa's party wins 31 percent nationally.
rejected.excerpt: With 99 percent of votes counted, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s party wins 31 percent nationally. South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC) party faces a major setback after last week’s municipal elections, leaving it in a weak position in coalition talks to form city governments. With 99 percent of the votes counted on Sunday, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s ANC had 31 percent nationally against 25 percent for its main rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA). That represents a drop of roughly 14 percentage points from its 2021 local elections performance. Former President Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe party won about 10 percent of votes, putting it in third place, while the rest of the ballots were split between hundreds of smaller parties. Final results are expected to be announced at 6pm (16:00 GMT) on Sunday. rejected.title: Egypt’s reopening of its embassy in Tripoli signals regional shift on Libya
rejected.description: Former rivals in Libya are pushing for a unity government to end years of conflict.
rejected.excerpt: Former rivals in Libya are pushing for a unity government to end years of conflict. The reopening of the Egyptian embassy in Tripoli marks a fundamental political shift, both domestically and regionally, for Libya, analysts say. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty inaugurated the historic embassy building on Saturday, which had been closed for 12 years due to security concerns. Libya has been politically divided since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, with rival administrations formed in Tripoli in the west and Tobruk and Benghazi in the east. Egypt was widely considered to be backing the eastern authority, effectively led by strongman and renegade military commander Khalifa Haftar, and his self-styled Libyan National Army (LNA), until recent regional developments led Cairo to rethink its approach.
